math-e1-l1.title: Counting
math-e1-l1.concept: Point to each object one at a time to find how many there are. Past 10, it is easier to count in groups of 5 or 10.

math-e1-l2.title: Addition and subtraction
math-e1-l2.concept: **Adding (+)** puts two numbers together. **Subtracting (-)** takes a smaller amount away from a bigger number.

math-e1-l3.title: Comparing numbers
math-e1-l3.concept: Use **>** when the first number is bigger and **<** when it is smaller. The sign opens toward the bigger number.

math-e1-l4.title: Shapes
math-e1-l4.concept: A **triangle** has 3 sides and a **quadrilateral** has 4 sides. A **circle** is round and has no corners.

math-e1-l5.title: Length and clocks
math-e1-l5.concept: We measure length in **cm**. On a clock, the short hand shows the 'hour' and the long hand shows the 'minutes'.
math-e1-l5.example: Short hand on 4, long hand on 12 → 4 o'clock

math-e2-l1.title: Place value
math-e2-l1.concept: In a 2-digit number, the left digit is in the **tens place** and the right digit is in the **ones place**. 10 groups of 10 make 100.

math-e2-l2.title: Adding and subtracting 2-digit numbers
math-e2-l2.concept: Work out the ones, then the tens. If a sum is more than 10, carry over. If you cannot subtract, regroup (borrow).

math-e2-l3.title: Meeting multiplication
math-e2-l3.concept: Adding the same number many times can be written in a short way with **multiplication (×)**.

math-e2-l4.title: Length and telling time
math-e2-l4.concept: **1m = 100cm**. Each time the long hand passes one number on the clock, 5 minutes go by.

math-e2-l5.title: Finding patterns
math-e2-l5.concept: Find the **pattern** of how the numbers go up or down, and you can tell the next number.

math-e3-l1.title: Multiplication and division
math-e3-l1.concept: Multiplication is adding the same number many times, and **division** is sharing equally. If you know your times tables, division is easy too.

math-e3-l2.title: Exploring fractions
math-e3-l2.concept: A **fraction** shows part of a whole that is split into equal parts. The bottom number is the **denominator** and the top number is the **numerator**.

math-e3-l3.title: Length, capacity and weight
math-e3-l3.concept: **1km = 1000m**, **1L = 1000mL**, **1kg = 1000g**. To change to the smaller unit, multiply by 1000.

math-e3-l4.title: Circles and angles
math-e3-l4.concept: A **right angle** is 90°. In a circle, the **diameter** is 2 times the **radius**.

math-e3-l5.title: Tables and graphs
math-e3-l5.concept: Put survey results in a table to easily see the most, the least and the total.

math-e4-l1.title: Large numbers
math-e4-l1.concept: Read and write large numbers in groups of ten thousand (10000). Each digit shows a value given by its **place value**.

math-e4-l2.title: Multiplying and dividing large numbers
math-e4-l2.concept: Split the number you multiply by, multiply each part, then add. For division, estimate the quotient and check it.

math-e4-l3.title: Adding and subtracting fractions and decimals
math-e4-l3.concept: For fractions with the same denominator, add or subtract **the numerators**. For decimals, line up the decimal points before you calculate.

math-e4-l4.title: Angles and shapes
math-e4-l4.concept: The three angles of a triangle add up to **180°**, and the four angles of a quadrilateral add up to **360°**.

math-e4-l5.title: Bar graphs and averages
math-e4-l5.concept: Read the data to find totals and differences. The **average** is the total divided by how many values there are.

math-e5-l1.title: Adding and subtracting unlike fractions
math-e5-l1.concept: If the denominators are different, first find a **common denominator**. Using the least common multiple of the two denominators is easiest.

math-e5-l2.title: Multiplying decimals
math-e5-l2.concept: Ignore the decimal points and multiply like whole numbers. Then put the decimal point back so the answer has as many decimal places as the numbers you multiplied.

math-e5-l3.title: Factors and multiples
math-e5-l3.concept: A **factor** of a number divides it with no remainder. A **multiple** is the number times 1, 2, 3...

math-e5-l4.title: Area and volume
math-e5-l4.concept: Rectangle: **length × width**; triangle: **base × height ÷ 2**; volume of a cuboid: **length × width × height**.

math-e5-l5.title: Ratios and rates
math-e5-l5.concept: A **rate** is the compared amount divided by the base amount. Multiply a rate by 100 to get a **percentage (%)**.

math-e6-l1.title: Multiplying and dividing fractions and decimals
math-e6-l1.concept: To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators. To divide by a fraction, multiply by its **reciprocal**.

math-e6-l2.title: Proportions and sharing in a ratio
math-e6-l2.concept: In a proportion, **product of the inner terms = product of the outer terms**. Sharing a total in a given ratio is called **proportional sharing**.

math-e6-l3.title: Percentages
math-e6-l3.concept: A **percentage (%)** is a rate when the base amount is taken as 100. Multiply a decimal by 100 to get a %.

math-e6-l4.title: Circles and solid shapes
math-e6-l4.concept: The circumference of a circle is **diameter × 3.14**, and the area of a circle is **radius × radius × 3.14**.

math-e6-l5.title: Averages and organising data
math-e6-l5.concept: The **mean** is total ÷ count, the **median** is the middle number, and the **mode** is the number that appears most often.

math-h1-l1.title: Polynomial division and the remainder theorem
math-h1-l1.concept: The remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x-a$ is $P(a)$, and if $P(a)=0$ then $x-a$ is a factor.

math-h1-l2.title: Complex numbers and the discriminant
math-h1-l2.concept: $i^2=-1$, and if the discriminant $D=b^2-4ac<0$ the equation has imaginary roots. Imaginary roots of a quadratic equation with real coefficients come in complex conjugate pairs.

math-h1-l3.title: Quadratic inequalities
math-h1-l3.concept: Read the solution from where the graph of the quadratic function lies compared with the $x$-axis. $(x-a)(x-b)<0$ means between the two roots, and $>0$ means outside them.

math-h1-l4.title: Permutations and combinations
math-h1-l4.concept: If order matters, use permutations $_nP_r$; if not, use combinations $_nC_r$. For 'at least one', subtract the complement from the total.

math-h1-l5.title: Equations of lines and circles
math-h1-l5.concept: Distance from a point to a line $\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2} }$, circle $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$, and a tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
math-h1-l5.example: Slope of the tangent to the circle $x^2+y^2=25$ at the point $(3,\ 4)$ $=-\frac34$

math-h2-l1.title: Exponents and logarithms
math-h2-l1.concept: $\log_a b=x \iff a^x=b$. A sum of logs is the log of a product, and a difference is the log of a quotient. Exponential growth is written as $a\cdot r^t$.

math-h2-l2.title: Trigonometric functions
math-h2-l2.concept: $\pi$ radians $=180^\circ$. The signs of $\sin,\ \cos,\ \tan$ change from quadrant to quadrant. $y=a\sin bx+c$ has maximum value $|a|+c$ and period $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$.

math-h2-l3.title: Arithmetic and geometric sequences
math-h2-l3.concept: $a_n=a+(n-1)d$, $a_n=ar^{n-1}$. The sum of an arithmetic sequence is $S_n=\frac{n(a+l)}{2}$.

math-h2-l4.title: Limits and continuity
math-h2-l4.concept: For the form $\frac00$, factorise and cancel. As $x\to\infty$, divide by the highest-degree term. A function is continuous when the left limit, right limit and function value are all equal.

math-h2-l5.title: Differentiation and its uses
math-h2-l5.concept: $(x^n)'=nx^{n-1}$. $f'(a)$ is the slope of the tangent, and the sign of $f'$ tells you where the function increases or decreases and where it has extreme values. Velocity is the derivative of position.

math-h3-l1.title: Indefinite and definite integrals
math-h3-l1.concept: $\int x^n dx=\frac{x^{n+1} }{n+1}+C$, $\int_a^b f(x)dx=F(b)-F(a)$. Swapping the upper and lower limits changes the sign, and the interval can be split.

math-h3-l2.title: Using definite integrals
math-h3-l2.concept: For area, integrate $|f(x)|$. Split off the parts of the graph below the $x$-axis, and between two curves integrate (upper)−(lower). Integrating velocity gives the distance travelled.

math-h3-l3.title: Geometric series
math-h3-l3.concept: If $|r|<1$, it converges: $\sum ar^{n-1}=\frac{a}{1-r}$; if $|r|\ge 1$, it diverges. It is used for repeating decimals and repeating motion.

math-h3-l4.title: Conditional probability and independence
math-h3-l4.concept: $P(B\mid A)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(A)}$. If the events are independent, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$, and for independent trials the probability is $_nC_k\,p^k(1-p)^{n-k}$.

math-h3-l5.title: Binomial and normal distributions
math-h3-l5.concept: The mean of $B(n,p)$ is $np$ and the variance is $np(1-p)$. Standardise a normal distribution with $Z=\frac{X-m}{\sigma}$; it is symmetric about the mean.

math-l1.title: Finding the value of an expression
math-l1.concept: Putting a number in place of a letter is called **substitution**. The result you get is the **value of the expression**. When you substitute a negative number, use brackets to avoid mistakes.

math-l2.title: Properties of equality
math-l2.concept: An equation is like a **balance scale**. If you add or subtract the same number on both sides, or multiply or divide both sides by the same number (not 0), the scale stays balanced.
math-l2.example: Subtract $5$ from both sides of $x+5=9$ to get $x=4$.

math-l3.title: Solving linear equations
math-l3.concept: Move the terms with $x$ to one side and the numbers to the other side (**transposing**). A term changes its sign when it moves across. Finally, divide by the number in front of $x$ and you are done!

math-l4.title: Solving problems with equations
math-l4.concept: For word problems: **let $x$ be what you want to find** → turn the sentence into an equation → solve it → check that the answer fits the conditions.

math-m2-l1.title: Laws of exponents and polynomials
math-m2-l1.concept: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents. For a power of a power, multiply the exponents. For polynomials, combine like terms.

math-m2-l2.title: Systems of linear equations
math-m2-l2.concept: Eliminate one letter from the two equations to find the solution. Choose elimination or substitution to suit the problem.

math-m2-l3.title: Linear inequalities
math-m2-l3.concept: Solve them like equations, but when you multiply or divide by a negative number, the inequality sign flips.

math-m2-l4.title: Linear functions and graphs
math-m2-l4.concept: In $y=ax+b$, $a$ is the slope and $b$ is the $y$-intercept. Parallel lines have the same slope.

math-m2-l5.title: Counting and probability
math-m2-l5.concept: Probability = (number of favourable outcomes) ÷ (number of all outcomes). Multiply for independent events that happen together, and use the complement for 'at least'.

math-m3-l1.title: Square roots and real numbers
math-m3-l1.concept: $\sqrt{a}$ is the non-negative number whose square is $a$. Take square factors out of the root sign, and rationalise roots in the denominator.

math-m3-l2.title: Multiplication formulas and factorisation
math-m3-l2.concept: $(a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2$, $(a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2$. Factorising means using these formulas in reverse.

math-m3-l3.title: Quadratic equations
math-m3-l3.concept: Factorise to get the form $AB=0$ and solve. The discriminant $D=b^2-4ac$ tells you how many roots there are, and you can also use the relationship between roots and coefficients.

math-m3-l4.title: Quadratic functions and graphs
math-m3-l4.concept: The vertex of $y=a(x-p)^2+q$ is $(p,\ q)$, and the sign of $a$ decides which way the graph opens. Complete the square to find the vertex.

math-m3-l5.title: Trigonometric ratios
math-m3-l5.concept: In a right triangle, $\sin A=\frac{\text{opposite} }{\text{hypotenuse} }$, $\cos A=\frac{\text{adjacent} }{\text{hypotenuse} }$, $\tan A=\frac{\text{opposite} }{\text{adjacent} }$.

math-e1-geo1.title: Shape names and corners
math-e1-geo1.concept: A **triangle** has 3 sides and a **quadrilateral** has 4 sides. A **circle** is round and has no corners.

math-e1-geo2.title: Solid shapes
math-e1-geo2.concept: A box shape is a **cuboid**, a round pillar is a **cylinder**, and a ball is a **sphere**.

math-e2-geo1.title: Triangles and quadrilaterals
math-e2-geo1.concept: A **triangle** has 3 straight sides and 3 corners; a **quadrilateral** has 4 straight sides and 4 corners, whatever its shape. Their number of sides equals their number of corners.

math-e2-geo2.title: Length and time
math-e2-geo2.concept: Put one end at 0 on the ruler; the mark at the other end is the length. $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$. Multiply the number the long hand points to by 5 to get the minutes.

math-e3-geo1.title: Angles and right angles
math-e3-geo1.concept: Two rays from one point form an **angle**. A $90^\circ$ angle is a **right angle**; smaller is **acute**, larger is **obtuse**.

math-e3-geo2.title: Radius and diameter
math-e3-geo2.concept: The **radius** goes from the centre to the circle; the **diameter** passes through the centre. The diameter is twice the radius.

math-e4-geo1.title: Angle sums
math-e4-geo1.concept: The three angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$ and the four angles of a quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$.

math-e4-geo2.title: Quadrilaterals and polygons
math-e4-geo2.concept: One pair of parallel sides makes a **trapezoid**, two pairs a **parallelogram**, and four equal sides a **rhombus**. A **diagonal** joins two vertices that are not neighbours.

math-e5-geo1.title: Perimeter and area
math-e5-geo1.concept: Rectangle: width × height. Triangle: base × height ÷ 2. Parallelogram: base × height. Trapezoid: (top + bottom) × height ÷ 2. Rhombus: diagonal × diagonal ÷ 2.

math-e5-geo2.title: Congruence and symmetry
math-e5-geo2.concept: Two shapes that match exactly are **congruent**. A shape that folds onto itself along a line is **symmetric**; that line is the **line of symmetry**.
math-e5-geo2.example: A square has 4 lines of symmetry

math-e6-geo1.title: Circumference and circle area
math-e6-geo1.concept: Circumference = diameter × π, area = radius × radius × π, with π ≈ $3.14$.

math-e6-geo2.title: Cuboids and cubes
math-e6-geo2.concept: Volume = length × width × height; surface area = (sum of three face areas) × 2. A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

math-m1-geo1.title: Angle rules and polygons
math-m1-geo1.concept: Vertically opposite angles are equal; corresponding and alternate angles on parallel lines are equal. The interior angles of an $n$-sided polygon add up to $180^\circ\times(n-2)$.

math-m1-geo2.title: Sectors and solids
math-m1-geo2.concept: Arc length $=2\pi r\times\frac{a}{360}$, sector area $=\pi r^2\times\frac{a}{360}$, sphere volume $=\frac43\pi r^3$, cone volume $=\frac13\pi r^2h$.

math-m2-geo1.title: Triangles and quadrilaterals
math-m2-geo1.concept: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to $180^\circ$, and the segment joining two midpoints of a triangle is half the third side.

math-m2-geo2.title: Similarity and the Pythagorean theorem
math-m2-geo2.concept: Similar figures have equal side ratios and their areas are in the square of that ratio. In a right triangle $a^2+b^2=c^2$.

math-m3-geo1.title: Trigonometric ratios
math-m3-geo1.concept: In a right triangle $\sin A$ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, $\cos A$ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, $\tan A$ = opposite ÷ adjacent.

math-m3-geo2.title: Properties of circles
math-m3-geo2.concept: An inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius, and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to $180^\circ$.

math-h1-geo1.title: Figures on the coordinate plane
math-h1-geo1.concept: Distance $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$, midpoint = average of coordinates, slope $\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$.

math-h1-geo2.title: Equation of a circle
math-h1-geo2.concept: A circle with centre $(a, b)$ and radius $r$ is $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$. The distance from $(x_0,y_0)$ to $ax+by+c=0$ is $\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2} }$.

math-h2-geo1.title: Triangles and trigonometric functions
math-h2-geo1.concept: Law of sines $\frac{a}{\sin A}=2R$, law of cosines $c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C$, triangle area $\frac12ab\sin C$.

math-h2-geo2.title: Radians and sectors
math-h2-geo2.concept: $180^\circ=\pi$ radians. A sector with radius $r$ and angle $\theta$ (radians) has arc length $r\theta$ and area $\frac12r^2\theta$.

math-h3-geo1.title: Conic sections
math-h3-geo1.concept: The parabola $y^2=4px$ has focus $(p,0)$; for the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $c^2=a^2-b^2$; for the hyperbola $c^2=a^2+b^2$.

math-h3-geo2.title: Plane vectors
math-h3-geo2.concept: The magnitude of $(x,y)$ is $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$; the dot product is $x_1x_2+y_1y_2$, and perpendicular vectors have dot product 0.

math-e2-dat1.title: Sorting and showing data in tables and graphs
math-e2-dat1.concept: Sort things by a rule and count them; a **table** or a **graph** lets you compare at a glance.

math-e4-dat1.title: Reading line graphs
math-e4-dat1.concept: A **line graph** shows how a value changes over time with points and lines. Going up means an increase, going down a decrease.
math-e4-dat1.example: 12 on day 1 → 20 on day 3: up by 8

math-e5-dat1.title: Finding the mean
math-e5-dat1.concept: The **mean** is the sum of the data divided by how many there are.

math-e5-dat2.title: Chance
math-e5-dat2.concept: The **chance** of an event is a number from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain): chance = (favourable cases) ÷ (all cases).
math-e5-dat2.example: 3 A-balls, 2 B-balls → chance of A is $\frac{3}{5}=0.6$

math-e6-dat1.title: Band graphs and pie charts
math-e6-dat1.concept: **Band graphs** and **pie charts** treat the whole as 100% and show each part's share. Part = whole × share.

math-m1-neg1.title: Integers and rational numbers
math-m1-neg1.concept: Same signs: add the absolute values. Different signs: subtract them and keep the sign of the larger. For × and ÷ the result is + if the signs match and − if not.

math-m1-fac1.title: Prime factorisation, GCD and LCM
math-m1-fac1.concept: Writing a number as a product of primes is **prime factorisation**. The largest shared divisor is the **greatest common divisor**, the smallest shared multiple the **least common multiple**.

math-m1-crd1.title: The coordinate plane
math-m1-crd1.concept: A point is written (x, y). The signs decide Quadrants 1–4, and reflecting in the x-axis flips the sign of y.

math-m1-prp1.title: Direct and inverse proportion
math-m1-prp1.concept: **Direct proportion** is y=ax and **inverse proportion** is $y=\frac{a}{x}$. In direct proportion y÷x is constant; in inverse proportion x×y is constant.

math-m1-sta1.title: Averages and relative frequency
math-m1-sta1.concept: The **median** is the middle value in order, the **mode** the most frequent value. **Relative frequency** = frequency ÷ total.

math-m2-rec1.title: Repeating decimals
math-m2-rec1.concept: A decimal whose digits repeat for ever is a **repeating decimal**; the repeating part is its **block**. A reduced fraction terminates only if its denominator has just the factors 2 and 5.

math-m2-lfn1.title: Linear functions and linear equations
math-m2-lfn1.concept: In y=ax+b, a is the slope and b the y-intercept. The intersection of two graphs is the solution of the two equations together.

math-e3-ari1.title: Adding and subtracting three-digit numbers
math-e3-ari1.concept: Work from the ones place. If a column adds up to 10 or more, **carry** to the next place; if you cannot subtract, **borrow** from the next place.

math-e6-ari1.title: Mixed calculations
math-e6-ari1.concept: When the four operations are mixed, work out **the brackets** first, then **multiplication and division**, and finally **addition and subtraction**, from left to right.

math-e6-ari2.title: Rounding up, down and to the nearest
math-e6-ari2.concept: **Rounding up** raises the number to the next multiple, **rounding down** drops the lower digits, and **rounding to the nearest** raises it only if the next digit is 5 or more.
math-e6-ari2.example: 3472 to a multiple of 100: up 3500, down 3400, nearest 3500

math-m3-sta1.title: Variance and standard deviation
math-m3-sta1.concept: The **deviation** is (value) − (mean). The **variance** is the mean of the squared deviations and the **standard deviation** is its positive square root. The larger it is, the more spread out the data are.

math-h2-seq1.title: Sums of sequences and ∑
math-h2-seq1.concept: $\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k$ means $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n$. Useful rules: $\sum k=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$, $\sum c=cn$ and $\sum(a_k+b_k)=\sum a_k+\sum b_k$.

math-h3-pro1.title: The addition rule and complements
math-h3-pro1.concept: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$. The probability of the complement is $P(A^c)=1-P(A)$.

math-el-econ1.title: Interest, exchange rates and tax
math-el-econ1.concept: Simple interest = principal × rate × years; compound amount = principal × (1 + rate)^years. An exchange rate is the value of 1 unit of a currency; tax is price × a percentage.

math-el-econ2.title: Demand, supply and optimisation
math-el-econ2.concept: Equilibrium is where the demand and supply curves meet. Maximum revenue R=pq and elasticity come from functions and derivatives.

math-el-ai1.title: Text and image data

math-el-ai2.title: Prediction and optimisation

math-el-job1.title: Unit conversion and ratios
math-el-job1.concept: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 hour = 60 minutes. Sale price = price × (1 − discount); mixing in the ratio a:b gives A a share of $\frac{a}{a+b}$.

math-el-job2.title: Area, counting and growth
math-el-job2.concept: Area gives the material needed, the product rule the number of pairs, and (increase) ÷ (first value) × 100 the growth rate.

math-el-cul1.title: Mathematics in art and daily life
math-el-cul1.concept: The golden ratio is about 1.618; a note one octave up has twice the frequency; 6 braille dots give $2^6-1=63$ patterns; a majority is more than half.

math-el-cul2.title: Mathematics in society and the environment
math-el-cul2.concept: Means and growth rates let you analyse social and environmental problems mathematically. Growth rate = (increase) ÷ (first value) × 100.

math-el-sta1.title: Statistical questions and samples
math-el-sta1.concept: The standard deviation is the square root of the mean of squared deviations (the variance). Samples are drawn by random, stratified, cluster or systematic sampling.

math-el-sta2.title: Estimation and hypothesis tests
math-el-sta2.concept: The 95% margin of error is $1.96\times\frac{σ}{\sqrt{n} }$. If $|z|$ of $z=\frac{\bar{x}-\mu}{σ/\sqrt{n} }$ is above 1.96, reject the null hypothesis at the 5% level.

math-el-res1.title: Research methods
math-el-res1.concept: A mathematics research project can use literature research, case studies, mathematical experiments or development research.
math-el-res1.example: Rolling dice to find a pattern → experiment

math-el-res2.title: Research steps and ethics
math-el-res2.concept: Research goes topic → plan → carry out → present → reflect. Citing sources and never altering results is research ethics.

math-h1-mat1.title: Matrices and their operations
math-h1-mat1.concept: A **matrix** is a rectangular arrangement of numbers. Addition, subtraction and scalar multiples work entry by entry; the (i, j) entry of a product $AB$ is the sum of the products of row i of $A$ and column j of $B$, taken in order.

math-h1-set1.title: Sets and propositions
math-h1-set1.concept: $n(A\cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A\cap B)$, and a set with n elements has $2^n$ subsets. The contrapositive of “if p then q” always has the same truth value as the statement, but the converse may not.

math-h1-fnc1.title: Composite and inverse functions
math-h1-fnc1.concept: The composite $(g\circ f)(x)=g(f(x))$ is worked from the inner function outwards. The inverse function satisfies $f^{-1}(y)=x$ whenever $f(x)=y$.

math-h1-pol1.title: Factorising and solving cubic and quartic equations
math-h1-pol1.concept: Solve a cubic or quartic equation by **factorising** it (synthetic division or a substitution helps) and finding the values that make each factor zero. Check a quadratic factor with its discriminant.

math-h3-cal1.title: Differentiating exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions
math-h3-cal1.concept: Differentiate a composite function as (derivative of the outer function)×(derivative of the inner function), and a quotient with $\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)'=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$. Also $(e^x)'=e^x$, $(\ln x)'=\frac{1}{x}$, $(\sin x)'=\cos x$ and $(\cos x)'=-\sin x$.

math-h3-cnt1.title: Permutations and combinations with repetition, and the binomial theorem
math-h3-cnt1.concept: The number of arrangements **with repetition** is the number of choices multiplied by itself once per place. With repeated items, divide the factorial of the total by the factorial of each repeat count; **combinations with repetition** give $_nH_r={}_{n+r-1}C_r$. In $(x+1)^n$ the coefficient of $x^k$ is $_nC_k$.
math-h3-cnt1.example: The letters aabbc can be arranged in $5!\div(2!\times2!)=30$ ways

m-h1-pol1-v1.prompt: What is the sum of all the real roots of $x^3-6x^2+11x-6=0$?

m-h1-pol1-v1.explanation: $(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)=0$, so the real roots are $1,\ 2,\ 3$ and their sum is 6.
